chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Abu Maryam al-Ansari said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who said: 'I will visit so-and-so to seek her offspring; she will be free (not bound by a specific condition of childbirth) after I visit her.' Is it permissible for him to visit her without ejaculating inside her? He said: 'When he visits her, he has sought her offspring.'
ai.seo_question: Does a man need to ejaculate inside his wife to fulfill the marital goal of having children according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the legal and spiritual objective of seeking offspring is fulfilled by the act of conjugal union (consummation) itself, regardless of whether ejaculation occurs inside the wife. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the mere act of intercourse establishes the fulfillment of the marital purpose, distinguishing between the physical act and the specific biological outcome of conception. It highlights the flexibility in marital intentions, allowing couples to pursue progeny without strict adherence to insemination as the sole criterion for achieving the goal.
